# Global Energy Storage Market to Grow 15-Fold by 2030
![](https://assets.bbhub.io/image/v1/resize?width=auto&type=webp&url=https://assets.bbhub.io/professional/sites/24/Energy-Storage-System-Aerial-View.jpg)

_New York_ _, October 12, 2022_– Energy storage installations around the world are projected to reach a cumulative 411 gigawatts (or 1,194 gigawatt-hours) by the end of 2030, according to the latest forecast from research company BloombergNEF (BNEF). That is 15 times the 27GW/56GWh of storage that was online at the end of 2021.

BNEF’s _2H 2022_ _Energy Storage Market Outlook_ sees an additional 13% of capacity by 2030 than previously estimated, primarily driven by recent policy developments. This is equal to an extra 46GW/145GWh.

An estimated 387GW/1,143GWh of new energy storage capacity will be added globally from 2022 to 2030 – more than Japan’s entire power generation capacity in 2020. The US and China are set to remain the two largest markets, representing over half of global storage installations by the end of the decade.

The anticipated acceleration of the US market follows the passage of the Inflation Reduction Act in August 2022, with large volumes of funds allocated to wind, solar and storage tax credits. The law will drive roughly 30GW/111GWh of energy storage build from 2022 to 2030, according to BNEF. However, while the new tax credit policy supports more growth based on BNEF’s long-term forecast, supply chain constraints cloud deployment expectations until 2024.

BNEF has more than doubleenergy storage deployments from 2025 to 2030 across Europe from previous forecasts.

Helen Kou, an energy storage associate at BNEF and lead author of the report, said: “The energy storage industry is facing growing pains. Yet, despite higher battery system prices, demand is clear. There will be over 1 terawatt-hour of energy capacity by 2030. The largest power markets in the world, like China, the US, India and the EU, have all passed legislation that incentivizes energy storage deployments.”

But the Americas will add more capacity on a megawatt-hour basis as storage plants in the US usually have more hours of storage.

![](https://assets.bbhub.io/professional/sites/24/BNEF-Figure-1-Global-cumulative-energy-storage-installations-2015-20301.png)

BNEF’s forecast suggests that the majority of energy storage build by 2030, equivalent to 61% of megawatts, will be to provide so-called energy shifting – in other words, advancing or delaying the time of electricity dispatch.

Customer-sited batteries ­– both residential, and commercial and industrial – are also expected to grow at a steady pace. Germany and Australia are currently the leaders in this space, with sizeable markets in Japan and California too. BNEF forecasts energy storage located in homes and businesses will make up about one quarter of global storage installations by 2030.

Yayoi Sekine, head of energy storage at BNEF, added: “With ambition the energy storage market has potential to pick-up incredibly quickly. However, companies are already scaling up operations to capture the upside.”

Rapidly evolving battery technology is driving the energy storage market. Lithium-ion batteries account for the majority of installations at present, but many non-battery technologies are under development, such as compressed air and thermal energy storage. Nevertheless, BNEF expects batteries to dominate the market at least until the 2030s, in large part due to their price competitiveness, established supply chain and significant track record.

_Note: BNEF’s definition of energy storage includes stationary batteries used in ancillary services, energy shifting, transmission and distribution grids investment deferral, customer-sited, and other applications._

- Global Battery Storage Additions: According to the IEA’s _Global Energy Review 2026_, global battery storage additions reached **108 GW in 2025**, increasing by **40% year on year** and setting a new annual deployment record.
- Utility-Scale Dominance: Utility-scale battery systems contributed around **87 GW**, or nearly **80%** of global additions in 2025, while residential, commercial and industrial systems represented the remaining share.
- U.S. Storage Deployment: According to SEIA’s February 2026 outlook, the United States installed a record **57.6 GWh** of energy storage in 2025, representing a **30% increase** over 2024.
- Standalone and Solar-Paired Storage: Standalone storage contributed nearly **30 GWh** of new U.S. capacity in 2025, while solar-paired systems added approximately **20 GWh**.
- Regional Deployment: According to the IEA, China added more than **63 GW** of battery capacity in 2025, followed by the United States with **19 GW**, Europe with approximately **6.2 GW**, and the Middle East with more than **3 GW**.
- Global Storage Volume: An energy industry assessment cited in 2026 estimated that global energy storage deployment reached **275.3 GWh** in 2025, representing a **61.3% increase** from the previous year.
- Energy-Shifting Applications: According to the IEA, more than **90%** of new battery storage projects in 2025 supported energy shifting and renewable-power balancing, compared with approximately **40% in 2015**.
- EV Battery Deployment: In May 2026, the IEA reported that global EV battery deployment reached approximately **1.2 TWh** in 2025.

## Report Overview
- _In May 2026, according to the International Energy Agency, **108 GW** of battery storage capacity was added worldwide during 2025, representing **40%** growth from 2024, while installed capacity reached eleven times its 2021 level. Around **80%** of 2025 additions were utility-scale, and [lithium iron phosphate batteries](https://market.us/report/global-lithium-iron-phosphate-batteries-market/) represented nearly **90%** of deployments because of their lower cost and suitability for frequent cycling._

The global Mobile Energy Storage System (MESS) market was valued at **US$7.6 billion in 2025** and is expected to reach approximately **US$22.8 billion by 2035**, growing at a **CAGR of 11.7% from 2026 to 2035**.

## Power Capacity Analysis
In 2025, **the 100–500 kW / 3,000–10,000 kWh** capacity segment held a dominant position in the global Mobile Energy Storage System (MESS) market, accounting for approximately **45.1%** of total revenue. Global battery storage additions reached **108 GW** in 2025, rising **40%** year over year and nearly **11** times compared with 2021.

The share of battery projects used for energy shifting also increased from around **40%** in 2015 to more than **90%** in 2025, showing the growing economic value of storing low-cost electricity and using it during expensive peak hours.

Battery-based UPS capacity also grew by **30%** to reach **45 GW** in 2025, further supporting smaller and modular mobile storage systems

# Energy Storage Market (2025 - 2035)
## Energy Storage Market Summary
The Energy Storage Market reached an estimated USD 32.4 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 39.2 billion in 2026 to USD 226.2 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 21.5% over the forecast period.

Utilities across the U.S. and Europe are retiring natural-gas peaker plants and replacing them with four-to-six-hour battery systems that stack arbitrage revenue with ancillary service payments.

North America is the fastest-growing region at a projected CAGR of 30.8%, propelled by federal incentives layered on top of state-level procurement targets in California, New York, and Texas.

## Key Report Takeaways
### • By Technology
- [Batteries](https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/battery-market-2930) commanded a 57.6% share of the Energy Storage Market in 2025, driven by LFP cell cost reductions and utility-scale procurement.

### • By Application
- [EV-charging infrastructure](https://www.marketresearchfuture.com/reports/electric-vehicle-charging-station-market-5401) storage is projected to grow at a 27.4% CAGR through 2035, propelled by corridor electrification programs.

### • By Region
- North America leads regional growth at a 30.8% CAGR, underpinned by IRA incentives and state-level storage mandates.
